There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

You can define virtual columns (not stored in the database). If defined, the Column name is the synonym of the SQL expression defined here. The SQL expression must be valid.
Example: "Updated-Created" would list the age of the entry in days
Define the custom style for header panel. For Example : background-color:gray;border:1px black solid;

format := {expression[logic]} ? {cssStyle} [,]
expression := @{context}@{operand}{value}
logic := {|}|{&}
cssStyle:= {color,background,font-style}
context := any global or window context
value := strings or numbers
logic operators := AND or OR with the previous result from left to right
operand := eq{=}, gt{>}, le{<}, not{~^!}
seprator:=, Examples:
@AD_Table_ID@=14 | @Language@!GERGER ? color:red;background:yellow;
@PriceLimit@>10 | @PriceList@>@PriceActual@? color:red
@Name@>J ? color:blue
@Age@>50?color:red,@Age@>20?color:blue
Strings may be in single quotes (optional)

The Record Sort No indicates the ascending sort sequence of the records. If the number is negative, the records are sorted descending. Example: A tab with C_DocType_ID (1), DocumentNo (-2) will be sorted ascending by document type and descending by document number (SQL: ORDER BY C_DocType, DocumentNo DESC)

The Document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed between greater than and less than symbols
If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field is empty if you create a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Maintain Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table (e.g. C_Order).

This field is used to specify or categorize the type of contracts, whether contract related to Account Payable and Account Receivable. This categorization helps streamline financial operations and reporting.
This field indicates the Contract Category according to the requirements, which can help to standardize contract management processes.
Summary of the terms of the contract.
The amount which has been utilized from the total amount of the Contract.

The Contract Amount field signifies the amount agreed upon between the parties involved in the contract. This figure can include all costs and charges associated with the contract, making it a crucial aspect of financial planning and tracking.
The Document Date indicates the date the document was generated. It may or may not be the same as the accounting date.

The Contract Start Date field is the date when the contract become effective and enforceable. It is the date from which the terms and conditions of the contract will apply and the obligations and responsibilities of the parties will commence.
The End Date indicates the last date in this range.
The publish button is used to complete the contract so that it can be used in further purchase or sales transactions.
Reference of base contract from which this new contract created.

This could be a customer, supplier, vendor, or any other type of business relationship. The selection of the business partner is integral to contract management, as it defines the counter parties involved and their roles in the agreement.
This field indicates the Business Partner Location for invoicing.

The user identifies a unique user in the system. This could be an internal user or a business partner contact. It Indicates the Business Partner’s user contact for invoicing. For e.g. For Organization or firm, invoice contact will be different than business partner. However in case of individual business partner invoice contact may be different.
Duration of the Contracts in years.
Duration of the Contracts in Months.
This process is used to renew the contract when it will expire.
If the contract is associated with a specific project or initiative within the organization, this field identifies the project, allowing for project-level tracking and reporting.
This field defines the pricing structure used within the contract. It can include details about product prices, discounts, and any price adjustments over time.
The currency field specifies the monetary unit in which all financial transactions within the contract are conducted. It ensures that all parties understand and agree on the currency in use.
This field outlines when and how payments are to be made. They may include due dates, payment methods, and any penalties or discounts for early or late payments.

The payment method field describes the means by which payments are to be made, such as wire transfer, credit card, or check. It streamlines the payment process and aligns it with the organization's financial systems.
Incoterms, or International Commercial Terms, are standardized trade terms that are recognized internationally and used in contracts for the sale of goods.
The status field tells the current state of the contract, such as whether its in drafted stage, completed or expired. It offers a quick overview of the contract's current position in its lifecycle.
This field indicates whether the contract has been formally approved and is legally binding. It serves as confirmation that the contract is valid and enforceable.
It Identifies Expired Contracts.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.
The "renewal type" field refers to the contract's renewal process. It indicating whether the contract renews automatically or requires manual renewal.
The renewal date field is the date when a decision about renewal must be made or when automatic renewal will occur.
The renewal term field describes the terms and conditions that apply during the renewed period. It may include any updates or changes to the original contract.
Specifies notice days, if customers don't want to renew his contract then customer must have to inform before notice days.
The number of cycles for renewing a contract refers to the number of times a contract can be renewed.
The date when the contract is terminated

It's essential for documenting the cause or circumstances that led to the contract's termination. Common termination reasons might include breach of contract, non-performance, change in business needs, or other relevant factors.
The date when the contract is terminated.
The Processed checkbox indicates that a document has been processed.

This field is used to define how the product is quantified. It specifies the unit in which the product is measured, such as each (for individual items), kilograms, liters, or any other relevant unit.
It is typically used to represent the monetary value of the product or charge that is associated with the contract being made or created.
It can be used to give more context or information about the product/charge being procured or supplied. This can include specifications, features, or any other pertinent details.

Customer Code allows you to a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave customer code empty, the system automatically creates a numeric code. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Maintain Sequence" screen with the name "DocumentNo_", where TableName is the actual name of the table (e.g. C_Order).

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

A Business Partner Registration Number (BPRN) is a unique identification number assigned to a business partner or Customer by a company or government agency. The BPRN is used to identify the business partner in various transactions, such as Sales orders, invoices, and payments.

The Sales Region indicates a specific area of sales coverage.

The user can see details such the username, address, phone number, and email address on the Customer Contact Details tab. The User locates a specific user within the system. A description is limited to 255 characters.

The Bank Account is essential for organizations that have to manage financial transactions and consumer payment processing. It helps ensure accurate and effective financial interactions with consumers by centralizing banking information, streamlining payment processing, and automating payment collection. The account number, bank name, and routing number represent some of the details that the user might discover about the Customer's bank account.
Credit Setting helps you to define level for maintaining the credit setting either for Customer only or for the customer Location(s).
If VAdvantage maintains credit status, the status "Credit OK" is moved to "Credit Watch" if the credit available reaches the percent entered. If not defined, 90% is used.

The Credit Limit indicates the total amount allowed 'on account' in primary accounting currency. If the Credit Limit is 0, no check is performed. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. If active, the status is set automatically set to Credit Hold, if the Total Open Balance is higher then the Credit Limit. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.
Credit Validation restrict or limit the scope for the transaction as per selected validation with respect to credit details.
The Rating is used to differentiate the importance

The Total Open Balance Amount is the calculated open item amount for Customer and Vendor activity. If the Balance is below zero, we owe the Business Partner. The amout is used for Credit Management. Invoices and Payment Allocations determine the Open Balance (i.e. not Orders or Payments).

The Credit Used indicates the total amount of open or unpaid invoices in primary accounting currency for the Business Partner. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.

The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

If you want to maintain different costs per organization (warehouse) or per Batch/Lot, you need to make sure that you define the costs for each of the organizations or batch/lot. The Costing Level is defined per Accounting Schema and can be overwritten by Product Category and Accounting Schema.

The Costing Method indicates how costs will be calculated (Standard, Average, Lifo,Fifo). The default costing method is defined on accounting schema level and can be optionally overwritten in the product category. The costing method cannot conflict with the Material Movement Policy (defined on Product Category).
The Posting Type Commitment is created when posting Purchase Orders; The Posting Type Reservation is created when posting Requisitions. This is used for budgetary control.
Determines if/when tax is corrected. Discount could be agreed or granted underpayments; Write-off may be partial or complete write-off.
The GAAP identifies the account principles that this accounting schema will adhere to.
You can define multiple cost types. A cost type selected in an Accounting Schema is used for accounting.

When checked, the system will not post any variances between the Purchase Order price and the actual invoice price. Use this option if you do not want to track or report these variances in your accounting records.

If the invoice is based on an item with a list price, the amount based on the list price and the discount is posted instead of the net amount. Example: Quantity 10 - List Price: 20 - Actual Price: 17 If selected for a sales invoice 200 is posted to Product Revenue and 30 to Discount Granted - rather than 170 to Product Revenue. The same applies to vendor invoices.
If selcted, you will post service related revenue to a different receiveables account and service related cost to a different payables account.

When selected, landed costs are initially posted to the account in the line and then reversed through postings to the cost adjustment accounts. If not selected, landed costs are directly posted to the cost adjustment accounts.
In the Automatic Period Control, periods are opened and closed based on the current date. If the Manual alternative is activated, you have to open and close periods explicitly.
If Costing value is False than Accounting Schema will appear in Amount Dimension Control
The Period indicates an exclusive range of dates for a calendar.

If Automatic Period Control is enabled, the current period is calculated based on the system date and you can always post to all days in the current period. History Days enable to post to previous periods. E.g. today is May 15th and History Days is set to 30, you can post back to April 15th

If Automatic Period Control is enabled, the current period is calculated based on the system date and you can always post to all days in the current period. Future Days enable to post to future periods. E.g. today is Apr 15th and Future Days is set to 30, you can post up to May 15th
For Invoice costing methods, you can adjust the cost of goods sold. At the time of shipment, you may not have received the invoice for the receipt or cost adjustments like freight, customs, etc.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

If this vendor is used with another organization which is linked with other Business Partner in the system, so when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.
Withholding applicable on AP Invoice indicates whether withholding should be applied to AP invoices for specific vendor, when this is true system will apply withholding tax while creating AP invoice.
This field represents that withholding tax to be calculated on the AP Payment

AP withholding tax, also known as Accounts Payable withholding tax, is a tax that is imposed on payments made to vendors or suppliers by a company. The tax is withheld by the company at the time of payment and is then remitted to the government on behalf of the vendor or supplier.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The Mail Template indicates the mail template for return messages. Mail text can include variables. The priority of parsing is User/Contact, Account and then the underlying business object (like Request, Dunning, Workflow object).
So, @Name@ would resolve into the User name (if user is defined defined), then Account name (if Account is defined) and then the Name of the business object if it has a Name.

A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The Document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed between greater than and less than symbols
If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field is empty if you create a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Maintain Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table (e.g. C_Order).

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.
The Order is a control document. The Order is complete when the quantity ordered is the same as the quantity invoiced.

User can Apply the Overall Discount, Amount wise or Percentage wise on the Sub Total of the record & distributed Discount among all the Lines of the record. By selecting Clear Discount check box & clicking OK, will clear the Applied Discount amount with % and revert the original Line amount along with Discount %. Total Discount = (Apply Discount Amount/Sub Total Amount)*100 Line Discount = (Line Amount * Total Discount)/100

The Document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed between greater than and less than symbols
If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field is empty if you create a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Maintain Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table (e.g. C_Order).

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.
A Client is a company or a legal entity. You cannot share data between Clients. Tenant is a synonym for Client.

A search key allows you a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number. The Actual Life Time Value is the recorded revenue in primary accounting currency generated by the Business Partner.
The Potential Life Time Value is the anticipated revenue in primary accounting currency to be generated by the Business Partner.
The Rating is used to differentiate the importance

The Credit Limit indicates the total amount allowed 'on account' in primary accounting currency. If the Credit Limit is 0, no check is performed. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. If active, the status is set automatically set to Credit Hold, if the Total Open Balance is higher then the Credit Limit. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.

The Credit Used indicates the total amount of open or unpaid invoices in primary accounting currency for the Business Partner. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

This column contains the geographical coordinates (latitude/longitude) of the location.

In order to avoid unnecessary use of non-standard characters and space, the following standard presentation is used:
0000N 00000W 0000S 00000E
where the two last digits refer to minutes and the two or three first digits indicate the degrees

UN/Locode is a combination of a 2-character country code and a 3-character location code, e.g. BEANR is known as the city of Antwerp (ANR) which is located in Belgium (BE).

See: http://www.unece.org/cefact/locode/service/main.htm

A search key allows you a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Maintain Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table (e.g. C_Order).

The SO Sub Type indicates the type of sales order this document refers to. This field only appears when the Document Base Type is Sales Order. The selection made here will determine which documents will be generated when an order is processed and which documents must be generated manually or in batches.
The following outlines this process.
SO Sub Type of Standard Order will generate just the Order document when the order is processed.
The Delivery Note, Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of Warehouse Order will generate the Order and Delivery Note.
The Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of Credit Order will generate the Order, Delivery Note and Invoice.
The Reciept must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of POS (Point of Sale) will generate all document

he Document Type for Invoice indicates the document type that will be used when an invoice is generated from this sales document. This field will display only when the base document type is Sales Order and the Pro Forma Invoice checkbox is selected

The Total Open Balance Amount is the calculated open item amount for Customer and Vendor activity. If the Balance is below zero, we owe the Business Partner. The amout is used for Credit Management. Invoices and Payment Allocations determine the Open Balance (i.e. not Orders or Payments).

The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

Miminum Shelf Life of products with Guarantee Date instance. If > 0 you cannot select products with a shelf life ((Guarantee Date-Today) / Guarantee Days) less than the minum shelf life, unless you select "Show All"

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. If active, the status is set automatically set to Credit Hold, if the Total Open Balance is higher then the Credit Limit. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

A search key allows you a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number. The name of an entity (record) is used as an default search option in addition to the search key. The name is up to 100 characters in length.

The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The Total Open Balance Amount is the calculated open item amount for Customer and Vendor activity. If the Balance is below zero, we owe the Business Partner. The amout is used for Credit Management. Invoices and Payment Allocations determine the Open Balance (i.e. not Orders or Payments).

The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

Miminum Shelf Life of products with Guarantee Date instance. If > 0 you cannot select products with a shelf life ((Guarantee Date-Today) / Guarantee Days) less than the minum shelf life, unless you select "Show All"

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. If active, the status is set automatically set to Credit Hold, if the Total Open Balance is higher then the Credit Limit. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.
A Client is a company or a legal entity. You cannot share data between Clients. Tenant is a synonym for Client.
An organization is a unit of your Tenant or legal entity - examples are store, department. You can share data between organizations.
A Customer/Prospect is anyone with whom you transact. This can include Vendor, Customer, Employee or Salesperson
The name of an entity (record) is used as an default search option in addition to the search key. The name is up to 100 characters in length.
A description is limited to 255 characters.

The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

The Total Open Balance Amount is the calculated open item amount for Customer and Vendor activity. If the Balance is below zero, we owe the Business Partner. The amout is used for Credit Management. Invoices and Payment Allocations determine the Open Balance (i.e. not Orders or Payments).

The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

Miminum Shelf Life of products with Guarantee Date instance. If > 0 you cannot select products with a shelf life ((Guarantee Date-Today) / Guarantee Days) less than the minum shelf life, unless you select "Show All"

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. If active, the status is set automatically set to Credit Hold, if the Total Open Balance is higher then the Credit Limit. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The business partner is another organization in the system. So when performing transactions, the counter-document is created automatically. Example: You have BPartnerA linked to OrgA and BPartnerB linked to OrgB. If you create a sales order for BPartnerB in OrgA a purchase order is created for BPartnerA in OrgB. This allows to have explicit documents for Inter-Org transactions.

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. If active, the status is set automatically set to Credit Hold, if the Total Open Balance is higher then the Credit Limit. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The List Price Min Margin indicates the minimum margin for a product. The margin is calculated by subtracting the original list price from the newly calculated price. If this field contains 0.00 then it is ignored.

The Standard Price Min Margin indicates the minimum margin for a product. The margin is calculated by subtracting the original Standard price from the newly calculated price. If this field contains 0.00 then it is ignored.
Indicates the minimum margin for a product. The margin is calculated by subtracting the original limit price from the newly calculated price. If this field contains 0.00 then it is ignored.
Formula Based

The List Price Max Margin indicates the maximum margin for a product. The margin is calculated by subtracting the original list price from the newly calculated price. If this field contains 0.00 then it is ignored.

The Standard Price Max Margin indicates the maximum margin for a product. The margin is calculated by subtracting the original Standard price from the newly calculated price. If this field contains 0.00 then it is ignored
Indicates the maximum margin for a product. The margin is calculated by subtracting the original limit price from the newly calculated price. If this field contains 0.00 then it is ignored.
Formula Based
The List Price Surcharge Amount indicates the amount to be added to the price prior to multiplication.
The Standard Price Surcharge Amount indicates the amount to be added to the price prior to multiplication.
Indicates the amount to be added to the Limit price prior to multiplication.
Formula Based
The List Price Rounding indicates how the final list price will be rounded.
The Standard Price Rounding indicates how the final Standard price will be rounded.
A drop down list box which indicates the rounding (if any) will apply to the final prices in this price list.
The List Price Discount Percentage indicates the percentage discount which will be subtracted from the base price. A negative amount indicates the percentage which will be added to the base price.

The Standard Price Discount Percentage indicates the percentage discount which will be subtracted from the base price. A negative amount indicates the percentage which will be added to the base price.
Indicates the discount in percent to be subtracted from base, if negative it will be added to base price

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Maintain Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table (e.g. C_Order).
